title: Cooling of US Midwest summer temperature extremes from cropland intensification

settings.description: US Midwest weather stations, June-August daily maximum temperature, 1910-2014, analysed by quantile regression and excluding the Dust Bowl of the 1930s and the 1970s-1990s aerosol cooling interval.
The 5th percentile of daily maximum temperature, evaluated separately.
The median of daily maximum temperature, evaluated separately.
The 95th percentile of daily maximum temperature, the extreme-heat metric of primary interest.
Trends recomputed from 1980 to 2014 to test whether the pattern survives the decline of aerosol forcing.
Total June-August precipitation trends, and stations grouped by precipitation trend above 3 mm per decade.
Areas with the greatest rates of land conversion to cropland since 1910, averaging about 3 per cent of grid cell area per decade.
Areas with the greatest cropland abandonment.
Counties with increases in irrigated area greater than 10 per cent of county area per decade, from agricultural census data.
Eastern Nebraska, where irrigation trends exceed 7 per cent of county area per decade.
Counties binned by trend in area-normalised crop net primary productivity, with the top bin exceeding 4.5 g C m-2 yr-1.
The intensification analysis restricted to stations with less than 10 per cent irrigated area, isolating rainfed cropland.
Counties with irrigation growth of at least 5 per cent of county area per decade, during months classified as drought by the self-calibrated Penman-Monteith Palmer index.
The same irrigated counties during non-drought months.
Rainfed counties with a NPPan trend above 2.5 g C m-2 yr-2, during drought months.
The same rainfed counties during non-drought months.
Assessment of the North Atlantic Oscillation index as an alternative explanation, including the post-1995 reversal.

claims.from: period 1910 to 2014 in the US Midwest
claims.statement: The hottest growing-season temperatures in the US Midwest have cooled since 1910, against the overall US warming trend.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. The paper's baseline observation is missing; every extracted claim conditions cooling on a land-use driver.

claims.from: temperature percentile
claims.to: sign and magnitude of the trend
claims.statement: Cooling is strongest at the 95th percentile, less evident in median trends, and temperatures are generally warming at the 5th percentile.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This percentile dependence is the paper's key evidence for an evapotranspiration mechanism.

claims.from: exclusion of the Dust Bowl and the aerosol cooling interval, and restriction to 1980-2014
claims.statement: The trends are robust to excluding the 1930s Dust Bowl, to excluding the 1970s-1990s aerosol cooling period, and to focusing only on 1980-2014.

claims.from: period 1910 to 2014 in the upper Midwest
claims.statement: Summer precipitation increased over much of the upper Midwest during the same period.

claims.from: stations with precipitation trends above 3 mm per decade
claims.statement: Patterns of increased precipitation and 95th percentile cooling are co-located, with stations above 3 mm per decade corresponding significantly to cooling regions.

claims.from: highest rates of land conversion to cropland
claims.statement: Areas with the greatest rates of land conversion to cropland show no statistically significant cooling, contrary to the commonly proposed connection.

claims.from: highest rates of cropland abandonment
claims.statement: Areas with the greatest cropland abandonment have on average experienced significant cooling, contrary to the proposed connection with conversion.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This counterintuitive opposite-direction result is absent.

claims.from: increase in irrigated area above 10 per cent of county area per decade
claims.statement: Weather stations in counties whose irrigated area grew by more than 10 per cent of county area per decade show significant cooling of extreme summer temperatures.
claims.match_note: Extracted four times over. CL002, CL004, CL007 and CL008 all record irrigation expansion leading to cooling of summer temperature extremes with no distinguishing condition, so three of them are redundant.

claims.from: eastern Nebraska irrigation growth above 7 per cent of county area per decade
claims.statement: Where irrigation increases were largest, in eastern Nebraska, 95th percentile temperatures cooled at 0.30 C per decade.

claims.from: geographic extent of significant irrigation cooling
claims.to: share of the cooling area explained
claims.statement: Significant irrigation-associated cooling is found only in Nebraska, Arkansas and the western US, and accounts for only about 11 per cent of the 134 million hectares cooling at 0.2 C per decade or more.
claims.match_note: Not extracted, so the extracted irrigation claims carry no scope limit.

claims.from: county trend in area-normalised crop net primary productivity above 4.5 g C m-2 yr-1
claims.statement: Counties with NPPan trends above 4.5 g C m-2 yr-1 show highly significant cooling of 0.22 C per decade in 95th percentile temperatures.

claims.from: magnitude of the NPPan trend
claims.statement: Counties with sequentially lower NPPan trends show correspondingly smaller rates of cooling, a graded dose-response.

claims.from: rainfed cropland intensification with irrigated stations excluded
claims.statement: The intensification-cooling relation is robust to excluding locations with more than 10 per cent irrigated area, so it holds for rainfed cropland.

claims.from: increasing NPPan compared with increasing irrigation
claims.to: land area undergoing cooling of at least 0.2 C per decade
claims.statement: Increasing NPPan is associated with seven times more cooling land area than irrigation.
claims.match_note: Not extracted, so the relative importance of the two drivers is lost.

claims.from: irrigated areas during drought and non-drought months
claims.statement: Regions with large growth in irrigation show cooling regardless of drought status.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. This is the contrast that makes the rainfed drought result interpretable.

claims.from: rainfed intensified areas during non-drought versus drought months
claims.statement: Rainfed areas cool during non-drought conditions but show no cooling trend during drought.
claims.match_note: Extracted as the rainfed null result under drought.

claims.from: inadequate soil moisture during drought
claims.statement: Inadequate soil moisture eliminates the capacity for greater evapotranspiration, so modern drought events feature greater warming as baseline cooler temperatures revert to historically high extremes.

claims.from: drought versus non-drought years
claims.to: difference in fitted 95th percentile temperature trends
claims.statement: Differences between drought and non-drought trends reach approximately 3 C during 1988 and 2012.

claims.from: declining tropospheric aerosol forcing after 1980
claims.statement: Trends computed since 1980 show a cooling pattern similar to the longer-term trends despite diminishing aerosol influence.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. A rejected alternative explanation.

claims.from: North Atlantic Oscillation index
claims.statement: The reversal of the North Atlantic Oscillation trend after 1995 together with sustained recent cooling suggests it has little influence on the hottest growing-season temperatures.
claims.match_note: Not extracted. A second rejected alternative explanation.

claims.from: agricultural intensification raising evapotranspiration potential
claims.statement: The authors' preferred explanation is that intensification, including regional irrigation growth, cools through increased evapotranspiration, especially on the hottest days.

claims.from: increased evapotranspiration
claims.statement: The authors propose that increased evapotranspiration also raises precipitation and overall rates of water recycling in the region.
